  S7 (884,522) deg=5 - OVERRIDDEN from the tracer's 'crossing' to JUNCTION. inkmap.py at (884,522) w=26 shows the x~884 column running straight from y=496 to y=548 with no semicircular hop and no sideways jog; the rail crosses it at y~520-524. The tracer's hop score of 6.1 is an artefact of the middle rail's gentle upward slope across the sheet (left branch enters at y~523, right branch leaves at y~520), not a drawn hop. No solder dot either - the ink at the crossing is ~3px in both axes, i.e. plain stroke width. Ink prior therefore reads junction, and the drafter's own habit on this sheet agrees: every other column (S9 at x=380, S6/S8 at x=575/581, S10/S11 at x=716/733) T's onto the middle rail with no hop. Consequence of the other reading: the Diode#3 / Diode#15 midpoint would be a dangling 2-terminal node and the 4uH -> 2k -> GND leg would be cut off from the x~880 column, breaking the ladder pattern shared by all four columns.
  S12 (116,533) deg=4 - explicitly JUNCTION. Crop shows the GND(#9) stub, the middle rail, the V-AC bottom lead and the I-DC top lead all meeting at one point with a clean four-way cross; the reported hop=5.7 is again rail slope. A crossing reading would divorce GND from the rail and leave the source column floating, so it is electrically impossible.
